rubric: Every diagram came from a `diagrams_spec` entry in the prompt (never one you invented) and shows nothing the spec did not give it
Each file passes `check-diagram.mjs`, and `check-diagram-render.mjs` passes or says `SKIP` (stated in the final message, never reported as a pass)
Every WARN still printed has a one-line reason in the final message, or was fixed
Subtitle, notes and flow labels are in everyday words: no identifier, path, HTTP verb or engineering word, and every acronym spelled out on first use; the exact code name is on the card

A flow has at most 8 steps and 4 actors, starts at the leftmost actor, uses every actor, and each failing step says what the reader sees or what happens next; a branch is an either/or frame, not a second picture
Every edge and relation has a label; every card has a short label; a note is one point per line
The remove test was done: no card, step or wire the reader does not need
Anything unconfirmed is `verify: true`; a fact that did not check out went back to its author as a blocker, not guessed
Only the files named by the spec were written, and the template shell is unchanged
The final message ends with a valid JSON hand-off block

live_scenarios.input: The flow spec has a step that sends `loyalty_tier`, a field not in contract/schemas.md.
must: returns status blocked with a blockers[] entry owned by Architect naming loyalty_tier
must_not: keeps the field and guesses its meaning

live_scenarios.input: A flow spec labels a step `POST /orders` and the subtitle says `idempotency key on the payload`.
must: labels the step in plain words (for example Place order) and moves the exact request to the card or a note
rewrites the subtitle in everyday words
must_not: leaves a check-diagram WARN with no reason in the final message

live_scenarios.input: check-diagram-render.mjs prints SKIP because no Chrome or Edge is installed.
must: says the layout was not rendered in the final message
must_not: reports the render check as passed

live_scenarios.input: The spec's flow has an out-of-stock case beside the confirmed case.
must: draws the two cases as one either/or (group and option on the steps)
must_not: draws a second diagram for the failure case
nests a branch inside a branch
